annotations.title: Dihedral Reflection
annotations.subtitle: Double-Bounce Corner Reflector Saturation
annotations.description: Right-angled intersections between aircraft fuselages, wing roots, pylons, and vertical stabilizers act as retrodirective dihedral and trihedral corner reflectors. Incoming X-band radar pulses bounce twice off orthogonal aluminum skins and return phase-coherently directly toward the Umbra receiver, saturating the dynamic range (+0 to +5 dB).

annotations.title: Radar Shadow Void
annotations.subtitle: Slant-Range Occlusion & Fin Height Mensuration
annotations.description: Because Synthetic Aperture Radar is an active side-looking sensor, tall airframe structures (such as B-52H and C-5 Galaxy tail fins) block microwave illumination down-range. The length of the resulting pitch-black radar shadow void (L) directly reveals vertical structure height via H = L × tan(grazing_angle).

annotations.title: Specular Ground Scatter
annotations.subtitle: Mirror-Like Forward Reflection on Smooth Tarmac
annotations.description: At X-band wavelength (λ ≈ 3.1 cm), paved asphalt taxiways, aprons, and graded caliche hardpan have root-mean-square surface roughness smaller than λ / (8 sin θ_grazing). Incoming microwave energy reflects specularly away from the satellite like a mirror, making smooth tarmac appear pitch black next to high-backscatter airframes.
